text:
B: Hiii! Hi, I'm Holly!
A: Hello Holly, Karim. Sorry, give me one sec, I'm just, the lamp. There. Okay.
B: You're fine! How are you doing?
A: Good, good. Bit scattered. I just had a lovely chat with a countryside ranger about birds, so I'm feeling quite outdoorsy now, which is unusual for me.
B: [laughs] Same, I've just spoken to a woman whose dog has the same name as mine. And the same breed. And her husband's got the same job as mine. Like, I'm a bit freaked out.
A: That's statistically suspicious. What's the dog called?
B: Biscuit. Cockapoo.
A: Of course it is. So what do you do, Holly?
B: So I'm GM of a cocktail bar and small-plates restaurant in Chelmsford. It's part of a group, we've got five sites across Essex and Herts. Twenty-two staff, all the events, private hire, suppliers, that kind of thing.
A: Okay, now I'm interested, because suppliers is me. I'm commercial director at a food importer in Smethwick, Birmingham. Middle Eastern and Mediterranean stuff. We sell to independent shops and restaurants, and a lot of these new dessert cafés. Honestly, your photo, you looked like the marketing girls from the dessert brands I deal with. That's a compliment, by the way, they're the happiest people in the business.
B: Aw, I'll take that! What sort of things do you bring in?
A: Everything, really. Pomegranate molasses, sumac, Turkish snacks, pistachio cream, which went mental last year. I've got about forty jars rolling round my car right now.
B: Stop, pistachio cream! We literally did a pistachio espresso martini special and it sold out in like a weekend.
A: See, that's what I mean. I spotted that early. Our owners didn't believe me, two very cautious brothers. And then it took off and they acted like it was their idea.
B: Oh my god, that's so annoying. Do you know what I mean, though, that happens in hospitality all the time. You come up with the thing and the area manager presents it.
A: Exactly that. I'm the ideas guy. Someone else's business, though. One day, maybe, my own thing. I'd need someone who loves spreadsheets, because I don't.
B: Honestly, same. I sometimes think about opening my own bar with a friend, but I'm like, who's doing the money? Not me. [laughs] My assistant manager does half my stock counts, don't tell anyone.
A: [laughs] Mine's called Bev. She chases me for everything. My inbox is about four thousand.
B: Four thousand! Sorry, that's actually stressing me out.
A: It doesn't stress me out, that's the problem. So what's good in Chelmsford, then? Because I go round looking at new places for work. In Birmingham it's Digbeth, Ladypool Road.
B: There's a new bar opening I'm dying to check out, like, really dark, natural wine, tiny plates. I'll probably go on my one night off and spend the whole time looking at their menu for ideas.
A: That's what I do. I don't drink, but I'll sit there with a lemonade judging their olives.
B: [laughs] Do you not? I'd do you a proper mocktail, not the sad ones. Like an actual nice one.
A: You'd be the first. Most places give me orange juice in a fancy glass.
B: No, that's criminal. Okay, if you're ever in Chelmsford, come in, bring your pistachio stuff, and I'll
A: That's a deal, see, this is how I get all my best
